add_nodes.title: Ship heat shield turned around in three days
add_nodes.description: One Starship-class ship reaches 20 orbital flights and, at least once, flies twice within 72 hours, with heat-shield inspection and tile work done at the launch site. Achieved when flight records or the operator show both.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No ship has been caught or reflown: Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and splashed down. Musk expects the first ship and booster reflights at the end of 2026 or more likely early 2027. Mach33's base case has 18 flights per stack in 2030 and assumes later-generation stacks average 60 flights; Falcon 9 boosters that entered service in 2020 averaged 24 flights (Mach33, Sep 2026). Starfactory already uses specialized robots to install tiles and heat-shield pins (NASASpaceflight, Jan and Mar 2026).
add_nodes.pathway: P7 (exogenous launch clock; AI-math effect through damage and inspection models, P1->P6)
add_nodes.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
add_nodes.why: Reuse at the scale of the launch clock (hundreds of heavy flights a year by the mid-2030s, about $13/kg internal cost in Mach33's base case) rewards ships that turn around in days, and Mars-window and lunar tanker surges add demand. Chain (S2): five reflights with two-week heat-shield turnaround (hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield, 2030) -> reflight cleared from data (physclock-twin-reflight-clearance, 2030) -> inspect-by-exception from tile damage and fleet heating models (2029-31) -> pad-side refurbishment with under 1% of tiles replaced per flight -> a ship flies twice within 72 hours and reaches 20 flights, about 2034. A 72-hour turnaround leaves no time for teardown, so data-based clearance is a hard prerequisite. Falcon 9 took 8 years from first reflight (Mar 2017) to a 9-day record (Mar 2025), and its 2025 median was still 38 days. If a two-week ship record in 2030 falls 25-30% a year, 72 hours arrives about 2034-36. AI mathematics shortens the inspection list through damage and inspection models. S3 is a year ahead of S2 on the launch clock, so S3 has two years of slack by 2035 and is Medium at the low end; S2 has one year and is Low. S4 equals S3. A single 72-hour turnaround is a record that SpaceX can staff with people, and its tile and pin robots are already in S2 and S3. General-purpose robots matter for sustained fleet turnaround, which the trunk's cadence nodes also leave uncredited.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: The economics may never need a 72-hour ship turnaround, because a larger fleet flying every few weeks gives the same cadence, so SpaceX may not try. If the ceramic tile concept is a dead end for rapid reuse, a new heat-shield architecture resets the clock by years.
add_nodes.signpost: Flight records showing one ship launched twice within a week, then within 72 hours; SpaceX statements on tiles replaced per flight and on robotic tile work at the pad.
add_nodes.note_2035: This is the 2032-35 step of Starship heat-shield reuse. S3 and S4 are Medium with two years of slack and S2 is Low with one. S4 equals S3 because a one-off record can be staffed by people and the tile robots are already counted in S2 and S3.

add_nodes.title: AI-designed heat-shield material in regular service
add_nodes.description: An AI-designed TPS material, coating or ablator (as defined in materials-tps-new-material-flight) is the baseline material for a primary heat-shield zone (forebody, nose or windward acreage) of an operational reentry vehicle and has flown at least 3 missions in that role. Coupons and test tiles do not count.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No AI-designed TPS material has flown, even as a coupon (general). Varda makes its C-PICA heat shields in-house and lost W-4 on reentry in May 2026; W-6 flew Sandia material samples and NASA Ames instrumented tiles. Starship Flight 10 (Aug 2025) flew metallic and actively cooled test tiles. New U.S. arc-jet capacity is being built (Kratos Project Helios, 20-25 MW, awarded Oct 2025).
add_nodes.why: Chain (S2): the first AI-designed coupon flies (materials-tps-new-material-flight, 2030) -> arc-jet qualification of the full material with its bond and attachment (1-2 years; the arc-jet queue binds) -> production scale-up and lot acceptance (about a year) -> baseline on a commercial capsule or a reusable vehicle's windward zone -> three missions, about 2034. Uncrewed commercial operators need no certifier, which lifts the band above the P7 Speculative default; crewed use would be capped at Medium. S3 is a year earlier because AI-run test stands (physclock-ai-run-test-stands, High in S3) shorten arc-jet qualification and lot acceptance; the coupon year is the same in S2 and S3. S4 equals S3: robots speed specimen preparation, and arc-jet runs double first in S4 (hyper-35-arcjet-throughput-2x, 2033), but that lands as qualification ends, and flight heritage at small operators binds, so the gain stays under half a year.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators rarely change primary heat-shield materials, and after the W-4 loss and Artemis I's char loss they favor flight heritage. Gains from a new material may be small next to manufacturing, bonding and attachment.
add_nodes.signpost: A capsule maker or reusable-vehicle operator names an AI-designed material as the baseline for a primary heat-shield zone; arc-jet qualification reports for such a material.
add_nodes.note_2035: This extends the AI-material chain from a coupon to regular service in 2033-35. S3 is Medium on AI-run test stands and S2 is Low with one year of slack. S4 equals S3: faster S4 arc jets arrive as qualification ends, and operators want flight heritage.

add_nodes.title: First aerocapture into orbit around another planet
add_nodes.description: A funded spacecraft (science, relay or commercial) enters orbit around Mars, Venus or Titan with a single atmospheric pass as its planned orbit-insertion method. Earth demonstrations do not count.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Aerocapture has never flown. NASA ordered a $350k study of an Arc-based Earth aerocapture demonstration from Inversion (11 Sep 2026, to 30 Jun 2027). Uranus studies find MSL-heritage aeroshells adequate for aerocapture (NTRS 20240014677). Mars launch windows open about Apr 2033 and mid-2035 (arriving 2036). Venus windows come about every 19 months: late 2032 to early 2033 and about mid-2034 (general).
add_nodes.why: Chain (S3): an Earth aerocapture demonstration (hyper-aerocapture-demo, 2030 at the earliest, Low by 2035) -> a small Venus or Mars mission adopts aerocapture and is funded (2031) -> a 3-4 year build (NASA small missions take 4-6 years from selection to launch, general) -> launch in the mid-2034 Venus window -> capture in late 2034 or early 2035. The Apr 2033 Mars window works only if the go-ahead comes before the demo flies, and the mid-2035 Mars window arrives in 2036. S2 is a year later. AI makes guidance, dispersion and rarefied-flow analysis cheap, so a small team can carry the analysis load; funding and the demo's success bind. The band is the demo's chance (Low) times the chance a funded adopter launches by mid-2034, under 10% in every scenario. S4 equals S3 because capital and launch windows bind.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: After a demo, a first planetary use still needs a mission whose design closes only with aerocapture, and with cheap launch most small missions can carry extra propellant instead.
add_nodes.signpost: A Mars or Venus mission selection, or a commercial Mars relay, that baselines aerocapture for orbit insertion.
add_nodes.note_2035: The first planetary use needs the Earth demo, a funded mission, a 3-4 year build and a window, so the mid-2034 Venus window is the only realistic slot inside 2035. Every scenario is Speculative by 2035, and S4 equals S3.

add_nodes.title: Second heavy Mars lander lands near the first without ejecta damage
add_nodes.description: A second lander of 20 t or more, from the same launch window or a later one, lands intact on Mars within 1 km of an earlier lander, without disabling damage to it from plume or ejecta. This is the precision and keep-out an outpost cargo build-up needs.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No 20 t-class Mars landing has been attempted. Landing ellipses for Curiosity and Perseverance were about 20 x 7 km and 8 x 7 km (general). Apollo 12 landed about 160 m from Surveyor 3, and its exhaust sandblasted the probe (general). In Feb 2026 SpaceX put Mars about 5-7 years out behind a Moon-first priority.
add_nodes.pathway: P7 (launch windows; AI-math effect through guidance and plume-surface models)
add_nodes.why: Chain: first heavy landing (hyper-mars-heavy-landing, 2031 window at the earliest) -> site data and terrain-relative navigation from that flight -> a second ship targets the same site in the Apr 2033 window and arrives late 2033. A same-window pair in 2031 is possible but unlikely: a 2031 landing most likely rests on one ship, and the five-ship fueling campaign (prop-35-mars-window-fueling) is dated to the 2033 window. Landing within 1 km is routine precision for propulsive landers; the hard part is the keep-out. Apollo 12 landed about 160 m from Surveyor 3 and its exhaust sandblasted the probe, and a Starship-class plume on unprepared regolith throws far more. AI mathematics helps through plume-surface models (prop-psi-models) and guidance with proven convergence; windows and SpaceX's priorities set the date. The band is the first landing's chance by 2035 (Medium) times the chance a second lander lands close without damage, so Low in S2-S4. S1 is Speculative because its plume-surface models are Low by 2035, so landers keep farther apart. S4 equals S3 because orbital mechanics binds.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics barely changes the date; windows and SpaceX's priorities decide it. SpaceX may spread early landings across sites to scout, or keep landers several kilometres apart until a pad exists.
add_nodes.signpost: A SpaceX statement that a second Mars ship will target the first ship's site; published plume-ejecta keep-out distances for Starship-class landers on Mars.
add_nodes.note_2035: This is the 2033-window follow-on to the first heavy landing, and the plume-ejecta keep-out is what it tests. Windows bind, so every scenario shares the year and S4 equals S3.

add_nodes.title: A crewed vehicle flies a heat shield sized by probabilistic margins
add_nodes.description: A crewed reentry vehicle certified by NASA or another space agency flies a heat shield whose thickness was set to a reliability target with joint probabilistic margins, including a flight-calibrated model-form term, in place of stacked aerothermal factors.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: NASA practice stacks deterministic aerothermal factors and combines branches by root-sum-square (SRL design, IPPW 2026); the SRL alternative-margining study was preliminary, and SRL ended when Mars Sample Return received no FY2026 funding. Artemis I's char loss pushed NASA toward more margin; Artemis II flew a modified entry on the same shield design (10 Apr 2026).
add_nodes.why: Chain (S2): probabilistic sizing adopted on uncrewed vehicles (2029) -> flight-calibrated model-form bounds (2030) -> a credibility standard that covers AI-built analysis (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard, 2029) -> an agency margin policy that allows reliability-based sizing for crew (2031-32) -> a heat-shield block change on a crewed capsule (Orion, Dragon or a national crew vehicle): redesign, arc-jet qualification and crew certification, 3 years or more -> flight, about 2035. Precedent: from Artemis I's char loss (Dec 2022) to a modified shield on Artemis III took about 5 years (general), and the char-loss investigation alone took 121 arc-jet tests over 8 campaigns. The certifier must accept the method, so the band is capped at Medium, and after Artemis I crewed programs favor margin. S3 is a year earlier because its model-form bounds land a year earlier; the institutional steps run at the same pace in S2-S4. S3 and S4 are Low by 2035 and S2 is Speculative. S1 lacks the calibrated bounds in time. S4 equals S3 because institutions bind.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Crewed programs rarely trade heat-shield margin for mass, and a thinner crewed shield saves little that matters. Agencies may use the method for analysis while keeping stacked factors for sizing.
add_nodes.signpost: A NASA EDL or TPS margin-policy revision that allows reliability-based sizing for crewed vehicles; a crewed heat-shield redesign that cites it.
add_nodes.note_2035: This is where the margin chain meets crewed risk posture. Certifier acceptance and a crewed qualification of 3 years or more bind, so the first flight falls in 2034-35 at the earliest; S3 and S4 are Low by 2035, S2 is Speculative, and S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-entry (2026-10-07): horizon 2035 and S4 review. New node for the 2035 horizon. Regulatory cap Medium; no named mechanism for crewed TPS margins is in motion, so 2035 stays capped. | E-entry resolver (2026-10-07): [skeptic] Hard edge from physclock-credibility-evidence-standard added (a crewed certifier accepts AI-built margins only through such a standard); soft edge removed. Years S2 2034 -> 2035, S3/S4 2033 -> 2034 (1-2 years from policy to a flown crewed shield was too short against the ~5-year Artemis precedent). band_2035 S2 Low -> Speculative.

add_nodes.title: Arc-jet test runs per year double
add_nodes.description: U.S. arc-jet facilities together complete at least twice as many heat-shield test runs a year as in 2026, from added facilities and from automated model change, instrumentation and turnaround between runs. Achieved when NASA, DoD test-resource reports or facility operators show the doubling.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: The Ames Arc Jet Complex is NASA's only ground facility for reentry TPS testing, built in the 1960s-70s, with flat maintenance funding; in 2026 the 30 kW mARC II needed a cooling-sleeve fix to extend run times. Kratos Project Helios (a 20-25 MW arc jet plus a 200 kW fiber laser, $68.3M, awarded 23 Oct 2025 under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program) adds capacity. Surveyed experts rank more arc jets as the top hypersonic-materials test need (ETI via Air & Space Forces).
add_nodes.pathway: P7 (test infrastructure; S4 lever is robot labor at the facilities)
add_nodes.premise_tier: n/a (infrastructure throughput anchor, not an AI-math implication)
add_nodes.why: Arc-jet time is the experiment gate for this branch. The S4 review splits arc-jet queue time into about 40% labor (model change, instrumentation, between-run turnaround, maintenance), 25% physics (run time, cooling, pump-down, electrode wear) and 35% capital, power and institution. Capital caps the number of facilities in every scenario; within each facility the labor share is what S4 compresses. Chain (S2): new capacity such as Helios enters service in the late 2020s -> AI scheduling and instant data reduction (physclock-ai-run-test-stands, Medium in S2) -> runs per year about 1.5-1.8x by 2035 (judgment), so doubling is Low and no earlier than 2035. S3 2034: AI-run stands are High, but they leave article setup to people, so S3 stays Low. S4 2033: general-purpose robots do bench and test work from 2030-31 (robo-lab-bench-useful, robo-24x7-integration-test) and help build new stands; automated model insertion and turnaround raise runs per day per facility about 1.3-1.8x (estimate), and leading facilities reach 0.41-0.47 of 2026 queue time by 2035. S4 is Medium by 2035. The S4 credit meets all four conditions: runs per year are throughput-bound, robots are useful there from 2030-31, there is no hard prerequisite, and S3's AI-run stands leave setup to people. Arc-heater power, electrode life and facility capital cap each run in every scenario, and S4 raises test demand too. S1 falls after 2035.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Arc-jet operations are high-voltage, hazardous work at government facilities that adopt new practice slowly, so robots may reach them late. Run counts are rarely published, so the doubling may be hard to see, and defense hypersonics may take most of the added runs.
add_nodes.signpost: Kratos Helios in service; an arc-jet operator reporting automated model insertion or runs per day; NASA or DoD test-capacity reports showing run counts or test hours.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension and the branch's one S4 credit: S4 is a year ahead of S3 and Medium by 2035 because model change, instrumentation and turnaround are labor-bound steps that general robots take over from 2030-31. Arc-heater power, electrode life and facility capital still cap each run.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-entry resolver (2026-10-07): new node from the advocate review, tempered. The advocate's years (S2 2034, S3 2033, S4 2032) and band_2035 (Low/Medium/Medium/High) were moved one year later and one band lower in S3 and S4: the S4 review's typical-facility figure for 2035 (0.56-0.64 of 2026 queue time) does not reach a doubling without new capital, and arc-jet operators are government or typical firms, not robot-first. Tier 4 infrastructure in place of tier 1 (tier 1 holds mathematics).

add_nodes.title: People return from orbit on a reusable ship
add_nodes.description: A crew of at least two launches to orbit and returns to Earth aboard the ship of a fully reusable heavy launcher (Starship-class), which comes through entry on its reusable heat shield and lands for reuse, on a licensed flight. Capsules, and lunar landers that never reenter Earth's atmosphere, do not count.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No crew has flown on Starship. Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and splashed down; no ship has been caught or reflown. Starship has no launch escape system (general). Under NASA's HLS plan, crews transfer between Orion and Starship in lunar orbit, so no crew is planned to reenter Earth's atmosphere in a Starship (general). In Feb 2026 SpaceX shifted focus to a city on the Moon. The last crewed entries on a tiled reusable vehicle were Space Shuttle flights, which ended in 2011 after the 2003 Columbia loss (general).
add_nodes.pathway: P7 (exogenous launch clock; AI-math effect through tile damage models and reliability priors, P1->P6)
add_nodes.premise_tier: n/a (exogenous physical clock: not an AI-math implication, so the P7 Speculative default does not apply)
add_nodes.why: Without a launch escape system, the safety case is the vehicle's flight record. A zero-failure demonstration of 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence needs about 229 trials: 9.2 years at 25 flights a year, 2.3 years at 100 (S4 review). Chain (S2): 100+ heavy flights a year from 2030 (physclock-heavy-cadence-100) -> a long run of successful ship entries and landings by 2032-33 -> crew cabin, life support and an abort case -> an FAA license for a crewed flight -> first crewed orbital flight and landing, about 2034. Demand would come from SpaceX's Moon-first plan if it moves crews beyond the Orion-HLS handoff (judgment). AI mathematics enters through tile damage and fleet heating models, which make each entry better understood, and through model-based reliability priors (physclock-reliability-priors-credit), which can cut the flights needed. S3 is a year ahead on the launch clock and has two years of slack, so it is Medium by 2035; S2 has one year and is Low; S1 follows its later heat shield and cadence. A licensed crewed flight is capped at Medium. S4 equals S3: flight statistics and the operator's risk decision bind, and robots do not add flights.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: SpaceX may keep crews on Dragon and Orion through 2035 and fly Starship crews only to the Moon, never through Earth entry. One ship loss in the run-up resets the record, and the tile concept carries the Columbia shadow.
add_nodes.signpost: A SpaceX crewed Starship flight plan with a date; a run of 100 or more consecutive successful ship entries and landings; an FAA license application for a crewed Starship flight.
add_nodes.note_2035: New in the 2035 extension: the first people through entry on a reusable tiled ship since the Shuttle. S3 and S4 are Medium and S2 is Low; S4 equals S3 because flight statistics and risk acceptance bind.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-entry resolver (2026-10-07): new node from the advocate review. Kept the advocate's years and bands (S1 Speculative, S2 Low, S3/S4 Medium) except S1 >2035 -> 2035, since the trunk dates S1's 100-flight cadence to 2030 as in S2. Capped at Medium as a licensed crewed flight. Soft edge from capability-35-heavy-cadence-300 left to the integrator (trunk node).

patch.thesis: AI uncertainty analysis lets commercial capsules fly thinner heat shields around 2030 (base case, Medium). Ship heat shields reach five reflights by 2030. Three-day turnaround and crews on a reusable ship stay long shots in the base case by 2035. Mars landings, aerocapture and crewed margins wait on windows, budgets and certifiers. Robots (S4) speed only arc-jet testing.
